evals.prompt: I modified `.github/skills/create-relationship/SKILL.md`, `projects/shared/spec-context.c4`, `projects/payments/system-model.c4`, and `README.md`. What can be pushed back to the template, and what must stay local?
evals.expected_output: The response separates generic artifacts from project-specific files and requires a generalization/confidentiality review before push.
expectations: The response classifies `.github/skills/create-relationship/SKILL.md` and `projects/shared/spec-context.c4` as generic/syncable.
The response keeps `projects/payments/system-model.c4` and `README.md` out of template push.
The response asks to generalize and remove project names before push.
The response requires a confidentiality review before push.

evals.prompt: I improved `.github/skills/create-relationship/SKILL.md`. Give me the safe sequence to push this improvement to `c4-template` using a `sync/*` branch, while keeping confidentiality review before push.
evals.expected_output: The response follows the safe workflow: branch from `c4-template/main`, cherry-pick generic file, diff/confidentiality review, push from `sync/*`.
expectations: The response fetches `c4-template/main` and creates a `sync/*` branch from that base.
The response only picks the generic file from `main`.
The response requires diff/confidentiality review before `git push`.
The response pushes from a `sync/*` branch, not directly from `main`.

evals.prompt: I want to pull improvements from the template for `.github` and `projects/shared`. Which command should I run, and why `--squash`?
evals.expected_output: The response gives targeted subtree commands and explains that `--squash` keeps history compact.
expectations: The response provides `git fetch c4-template main`.
The response provides both `git subtree pull` commands targeting `.github` and `projects/shared`.
The response explains that `--squash` keeps history cleaner/more compact.
The response avoids suggesting pulls for project-specific files.

evals.prompt: I improved `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4` in this repo. Another project wants the same fix. How do I verify it is truly generic before pushing to `c4-template`?
evals.expected_output: The response requires a genericity/confidentiality audit, then a safe sync workflow from a dedicated branch.
expectations: The response requires an explicit audit to distinguish generic fix from project-specific need.
The response requests diff/confidentiality review before any push.
The response creates or uses a `sync/*` branch from `c4-template/main`, not from `main`.
The response includes a simple rollback plan if the fix turns out too local or regressive.
